# Import versus install

This page is for administrators who handle packages in Setup > Packages or with `ezpm`, and for developers who set
`install_type`. It answers the question that causes most confusion around packages: what is the difference between
importing and installing, and what do uninstall and remove leave behind?

## Contents

1. [Four verbs](#four-verbs)
2. [Import](#import)
3. [Install](#install)
4. [The install type](#the-install-type)
5. [Uninstall](#uninstall)
6. [Remove](#remove)
7. [Which tool does which](#which-tool-does-which)
8. [Common situations](#common-situations)
9. [Related pages](#related-pages)

## Four verbs

| Verb | Changes the repository | Changes the site | Code |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Import** | adds the package directory | no | `eZPackage::import()` |
| **Install** | no | yes: runs the install items | `eZPackage::install()` |
| **Uninstall** | no | yes: runs the uninstall of the items | `eZPackage::uninstall()`, the `package/uninstall` view |
| **Remove** | deletes the package directory | no | `eZPackage::remove()` |

The site is the database, `extension/`, `design/` and `settings/`; the repository is `var/storage/packages/`
([The local package repository](the-local-package-repository.md)).

## Import

Import takes an `.ezpkg` archive, checks it, and extracts it into `var/storage/packages/<vendor directory>/<name>/`.
After an import the package can be listed, viewed, exported and installed; nothing on the site has changed. Import
refuses a package whose name is invalid or that already exists (`STATUS_INVALID_NAME`, `STATUS_ALREADY_EXISTS`); the
setup wizard's downloads remove an older copy first when they must replace it. Details:
[The .ezpkg file](the-ezpkg-file.md#how-exponential-reads-an-archive).

## Install

Install runs the package on the site (`eZPackage::installUnaudited()`):

1. Install every package listed in `<requires>` first, recursively.
2. Stop here, successfully, when `install_type` is not `install`.
3. Run the `<install>` items in order, each in its own database transaction, each by its handler
   ([Install items and handlers](install-items-and-handlers.md)). The first failing item stops the install unless
   `continue-on-error` is set.
4. When every item succeeded, record the package as installed: a row in the `ezpackage` table with the name, the
   version `<number>-<release>` and the date.

Each install is recorded in the audit trail as `system.package.install`. With `as_drafts` (`ezpm install --as-drafts`,
**Install as drafts** in the administration) only content object items run, as drafts, and the package is not
marked installed, so it can be installed as drafts again
([install as drafts](../../../bc/6.0/package-json-format.md#install-as-drafts)).

> **Note**
> Installing a package again runs its items again; `install()` does not skip a package that is installed already.
> The administration's install page warns about this.

## The install type

`install_type` is an attribute of the root element: `<package ... install_type="import">`. It has two values:

| Value | Meaning | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `install` (the default when the attribute is missing) | The items are run on install; the package can be uninstalled | content class, content object and extension packages |
| `import` | The package is only kept in the repository: install runs its requirements but no items of its own, records nothing, and uninstall does nothing | every site package of the 6.0.15 index, and the 7x and `ezwebin_` / `ezflow_` site style packages |

For an `import` package the administration's package page says: "There is nothing to install here: this package
has the install type "import". A site package is imported by the setup wizard together with the packages it
requires, and is not installed on its own." After an upload, such a package opens on its page instead of the install
page. `ezpm create <name> <summary> <version> <install|import>` sets the value for a new package; anything else
becomes `install`.

## Uninstall

Uninstall only applies to a package with `install_type="install"` that is recorded as installed. It calls each
handler's `uninstall()` and then deletes the installed record.

- The administration's **Uninstall** (`/package/uninstall/<name>`) walks the `<uninstall>` items in reverse order,
  asks when a handler needs a decision (for example, removing a class that has objects), and needs the
  `package/install` policy for the package's type.
- `eZPackage::uninstall()` in PHP walks the items of `<install>`.
- `ezpm` has no uninstall command.

What is removed depends on the handler: classes, objects and extensions are removed; from 6.0.15 on also the files
the install created and nobody changed since; SQL and INI changes have
no uninstall of their own and stay. Uninstalling cannot be undone. Each uninstall of an installed package is recorded
in the audit trail as `system.package.uninstall`.

## Remove

Remove deletes the package directory from the repository and clears its installed record. It does **not** uninstall:
classes, content, extensions and files the package installed stay on the site, and the package can then no longer be
uninstalled from Setup > Packages. In the administration the confirmation page lists what goes, which packages require
it and whether the installer uses it as a source; see
[Packages guide, 9. Removing packages](../../../guides/packages.md#9-removing-packages). On the command line:
`php ezpm.php delete <name>` (aliases `del`, `remove`, `rm`).

## Which tool does which

| Tool | Import | Install | Uninstall | Remove |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Setup wizard, kickstarter, `exp:install` | the site package and its requirements | the requirements with `install_type="install"` | | |
| Setup > Packages | **Upload** (`package/upload`) | **Install** (`package/install/<name>`) | **Uninstall** (`package/uninstall/<name>`) | **Remove** on the list or the package page |
| `ezpm.php` | `import <file>` | `install <name>` | | `delete <name>` |
| ezupdate | fetches packages from package servers into the repository | | | |

The ezupdate part is described in [Fetching packages with ezupdate](../admin-gui/fetching-packages-with-ezupdate.md).

## Common situations

| You want to ... | Do |
|---|---|
| Have a site package available offline | import it and its requirements; do not install them |
| Add a content class package to a running site | import it, then install it |
| Replace an imported package with the server's newer one | remove it, then import the new archive |
| Undo an install | uninstall in Setup > Packages, before you remove the package |
| Clean up the repository | remove; the site keeps what was installed |
